scenes.text: Doctors just injected a patient with a virus that no evolution ever made.

The patient had an infection that beat every antibiotic. So doctors turned to phages, viruses that hunt bacteria and ignore human cells entirely. Medicine has used them for a century. The problem is finding one that fits your particular infection. That search can take months. This time, in October 2026, an AI lab designed the phage instead. Days, not months.

Antibiotics are a hammer. They flatten everything in reach, which is why bacteria keep learning to duck. A phage is a key, cut to one lock. For a hundred years we could only find keys already lying on the ground. Now we can cut them. And the same hands that cut a key can, in principle, cut a crowbar. Which is exactly the conversation this field is now forced to have.
